doors.note: US: 1 own door, the 'Wiederhoeft Showroom', 325 W 38th St, Suite 1601, New York 10018 — 'by appointment only', where the bridal department hosts private in-person client appointments; listed on the stockists page alongside Bergdorf Goodman and a past Miami trunk show. Counted on the same basis as Danielle Frankel; flag if appointment-only salons should be excluded. New York label.

craft_evidence.owned: showroom only — New York City showroom for appointments and corset fittings; no workroom located
craft_evidence.madein: ~98% (78 of 80 sampled pages say 'Made in New York'); 71 of 80 are made to order with a 24-week lead time
craft_evidence.heritage: dated — designer Jackson Wiederhoeft (Parsons 2016, then Thom Browne); debut collection October 2019; CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist 2022
craft_evidence.process: partly — bridal process described (appointment, corset fitting, 24-week made-to-order, alterations), not the making
craft_evidence.reasoning: Nearly every page says Made in New York and most pieces are made to order with a 24-week lead time, but no workroom, maker or mill is named. City-level making with nothing behind it is a 2, the same as Markarian. The case for 3: the made-to-order and fitting process is documented.
